hero.headline: Trump administration drops anti-weaponization fund after Senate GOP pushback
hero.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the Trump administration will abandon an $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund that faced mounting criticism from Senate Republicans and legal challenges. The decision removes a major obstacle to passing a $72 billion legislative package.

"We are not moving forward with the fund. Period," Blanche told House members, signaling the administration's reversal on the controversial initiative.

The fund, announced last month as part of a settlement in Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over leaked tax returns, was designed to compensate what the administration described as victims of politicized prosecutions. However, the proposal quickly drew fire from multiple directions. The fund lacked clear disclosure requirements about how money would be distributed and to whom, raising transparency concerns among Republicans who worried about potential political favoritism.

Senate Republicans, including Majority Leader John Thune, expressed particular alarm over the fund's structure and lack of oversight. Some GOP lawmakers pressed the White House to commit to abandoning the effort entirely. "I do think the best way to handle it is if the administration decides to shut the fund down themselves," Thune told reporters.

A significant source of Republican concern was the possibility that pardoned January 6 Capitol rioters could receive payments from the fund. Vice President Mike Pence called this prospect "deeply offensive" and said the sentiment was widely shared among Republicans and Americans generally.

The political backlash extended across the political spectrum. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer described the fund as "corruption in broad daylight" and vowed Democrats would force Senate Republicans to vote on measures to block payments. Several Democratic-led states, including California, Illinois, New York, and Connecticut, proposed measures to tax or block any distributions to their residents.

The administration also faced legal challenges. U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema in Virginia temporarily blocked the administration from transferring money from the fund after Democracy Forward filed a lawsuit seeking to dissolve it.

Some reports indicated the Justice Department had paused the program to comply with court orders, while Trump may have been reconsidering whether to continue pursuing the fund, multiple news outlets reported.

The reversal represents one of the few instances where Trump has yielded to pressure from Senate Republicans on a significant policy matter. The decision to abandon the fund removes a key barrier to advancing the broader legislative package, which Senate GOP leaders had indicated could not move forward with the fund included.

The episode illustrates ongoing tensions between the White House and Capitol Hill Republicans over spending priorities and executive authority, even as the party controls both branches of government. Senate Republicans have demonstrated willingness to challenge administration proposals they view as overreaching, particularly mechanisms involving discretionary funding that could bypass traditional appropriations oversight.

cards.headline: Iranian Drones Strike Kuwait Airport as US and Iran Exchange Attacks
cards.body:
Kuwait's main international airport sustained significant damage after Iranian drones struck a passenger terminal, killing one person and wounding several others. The attack came as part of an escalating series of military exchanges between the United States and Iran that continued to threaten diplomatic efforts aimed at establishing a ceasefire.

Kuwaiti defense officials described the incident as a deliberate act of aggression. "Criminal Iranian aggression resulted in significant material damage to the building and injuries," said Brigadier General Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan, a defense ministry spokesperson. Kuwaiti civil aviation authorities suspended air traffic following the strike and diverted arriving flights to alternative airports.

The Iranian attack followed a US military operation that struck an Iranian tanker near the Strait of Hormuz. The US military disabled the M/T Lexie, a Botswana-flagged vessel, by firing a missile at its engine after the crew ignored repeated warnings over a 24-hour period. American forces said the tanker was attempting to pass through international waters toward Iran's Kharg Island.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps responded by launching missiles and drones at US military positions in Bahrain, though the US military's Central Command denied that these strikes caused any damage. US forces also reported shooting down three Iranian attack drones aimed at civilian vessels in regional waters and conducted strikes against an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island.

The IRGC justified its response by claiming the initial US strike on the tanker constituted unprovoked aggression. The Iranian military said the strike damaged the vessel's engine room and warned that its retaliation should serve as a warning.

This latest exchange underscores the deteriorating diplomatic situation despite optimistic statements from US officials. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Senate Foreign Relations Committee that a deal with Iran remained within reach and claimed the Iranian government had agreed to discuss nuclear program aspects previously off the table.

However, Iran's position contradicts this assessment. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that any violation of a ceasefire on one front constitutes a violation across all fronts, explicitly linking negotiations to Israeli military operations in Lebanon. Iran has indicated it may suspend peace talks with the United States in protest of Israeli strikes there.

This represents the sixth vessel that US forces have disabled since beginning their blockade of Iran in April. The military said it had redirected 122 vessels attempting to enter or exit Iranian ports. Previous Iranian strikes targeted a military base in Kuwait that Tehran claimed was involved in US operations.

The continued military exchanges demonstrate both sides' willingness to pursue military action despite ongoing diplomatic channels, raising serious questions about prospects for achieving a lasting ceasefire agreement.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 10% Tariffs on Dozens of Countries
cards.teaser: The US proposed new tariffs of at least 10% on 59 countries and the European Union, citing forced labor concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced plans to impose tariffs of at least 10% on 59 countries and the European Union, citing forced labor trade practices. The proposal would target most major US trading partners, including Canada, Mexico, and European nations including the UK.

The administration separately proposed 25% tariffs on Brazil, alleging the country engages in trade practices that are "unreasonable" and restrict US commerce. Brazilian President Lula da Silva responded with indignation to the decision.

cards.headline: House Democrats divided over Lebanon war powers vote
cards.teaser: Rep. Rashida Tlaib's resolution to constrain Trump from joining Israel's war in Lebanon has sparked internal party conflict.
cards.body:
An upcoming House vote on restricting the Trump administration from joining Israel's war in Lebanon is sparking frustration among Democrats. Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the resolution, but some party members are upset about being forced to take a position on the contentious measure.

The internal conflict reflects broader disagreement within the Democratic Party over Middle East policy and war powers authority. The divisive vote could significantly impact the resolution's chances of passing with Democratic support.

cards.headline: Midwest farmers face economic pressure as tariffs and war costs mount
cards.teaser: Rising costs from Trump's tariffs and the Iran war are testing a key Republican voting bloc ahead of November's midterm elections.
cards.body:
Farmers in the Midwest are experiencing economic strain from President Trump's tariffs and rising costs related to the Iran war, creating uncertainty for a demographic that strongly backed Republicans in recent elections. Trump won all but 11 of 444 farming-dependent counties in 2024.

The economic pressures come as Republicans seek to maintain control of Congress in the November midterm elections. Farmers represent a key voting bloc in several competitive Midwest districts and states, where agricultural issues often determine electoral outcomes.

cards.headline: New Medicaid work requirements raise coverage concerns for low-income patients
cards.teaser: A rule explaining how states must implement work requirements may make it harder for sick people to maintain health coverage.
cards.body:
The administration released a rule guiding 42 states and Washington D.C. on implementing Medicaid work requirements. Critics worry the policy may make it harder for low-income sick people to maintain health coverage.

Republican lawmakers and administration officials have framed work requirements as a way to encourage employment among Medicaid recipients. The rule's implementation details—including how states will verify work activity and which exemptions will apply—will significantly affect people unable to meet the requirements.

cards.headline: Stock market reaches new record as AI companies drive gains
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 closed at another record high, with artificial intelligence stocks leading the rally.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 closed at another record high, with stock futures showing minimal movement following the gain. Artificial intelligence stocks continue to be the primary engine of the market rally, with these companies driving much of the broader index's recent strength.

Wall Street analysts point to the concentrated nature of current market gains, noting that the surge remains heavily focused on the AI sector rather than being broadly distributed across the market.

cards.headline: At Least 21 Killed in Delhi Hotel Fire
cards.teaser: A fire at a hotel in New Delhi killed at least 21 people and injured dozens more, with many victims being foreign nationals.
cards.body:
A fire at a hotel in a residential area of New Delhi killed at least 21 people and injured dozens more. The blaze tore through the building, trapping guests and causing extensive damage.

Many of the victims were South Asians who had traveled to India to receive medical treatment or to accompany relatives seeking care. Foreign nationals from neighboring countries were among those killed in the fire.

cards.headline: Drone Strike Kills Seven on Bus in Russian-Controlled Ukraine
cards.teaser: Seven people died after a drone hit a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-occupied Crimea.
cards.body:
Seven people were killed when a drone struck a bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-occupied Crimea, according to a Russian official. The attack targeted civilian transportation along a major route connecting Russia to the peninsula, which Russia annexed in 2014.

The strike occurred as Russia intensifies military operations across Ukraine. Ukrainian forces have also escalated attacks within Russian territory, including strikes on a naval base and oil terminal near St. Petersburg during a major Putin economic conference.

cards.headline: Protests Erupt in UK Over Death of Handcuffed Student
cards.teaser: The death of 18-year-old Henry Nowak, who died from a stab wound while handcuffed by police, has sparked protests and violence across the UK.
cards.body:
Protests broke out across the United Kingdom following the death of Henry Nowak, an 18-year-old student who was stabbed by Vickrum Digwa while handcuffed by police. BBC Verify analysed bodycam footage released by police showing key moments before Nowak's death.

The case has generated widespread outrage and debate over police procedures and accountability. The UK government condemned violence that occurred at some protests. A minister also criticized police anti-racism guidance in connection with the incident, fueling public discussion about law enforcement practices.

cards.headline: Ukraine Strikes St. Petersburg as Economic Forum Opens
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones targeted a navy base and oil terminal in the St. Petersburg region on the first day of a major Russian economic conference.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched drone strikes against energy and military targets in St. Petersburg early Wednesday, as Russia's annual economic forum opened in the city. According to President Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian forces targeted a navy base and an oil terminal in the region.

Several long-range drones struck oil storage facilities after Russian air defenses attempted to intercept them. The strikes caused significant explosions, with black smoke rising from the blazing oil terminal. The timing of the attack coincided with the start of Russia's flagship economic conference, where Putin is scheduled to speak on Friday.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 10% Tariffs on Dozens of Countries
cards.teaser: The US proposed new tariffs of at least 10% on 59 countries and the European Union, citing forced labor concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced plans to impose tariffs of at least 10% on 59 countries and the European Union, citing forced labor trade practices. The proposal would target most major US trading partners, including Canada, Mexico, and European nations including the UK.

The administration separately proposed 25% tariffs on Brazil, alleging the country engages in trade practices that are "unreasonable" and restrict US commerce. Brazilian President Lula da Silva responded with indignation to the decision.

cards.headline: Ukrainians Observe Daily Minute of Silence for War Dead
cards.teaser: Every day at 9 a.m., people across Ukraine pause for a minute of silence to honor those killed in the war with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainians observe a minute of silence each day at 9 a.m. to honor people killed during the war with Russia. The daily ritual has become a national practice as the conflict continues.

The moment of silence has been observed since 2014, when hostilities between Ukraine and Russia began. The practice allows Ukrainians across the country to collectively remember those who have died in the fighting. The ritual takes place in cities and towns throughout Ukraine at the same time each morning.

hero.headline: US and Iran exchange new strikes as Iranian drones hit Kuwait airport
hero.body:
Tensions between the United States and Iran escalated dramatically as both nations launched fresh military strikes, with Iranian drones damaging Kuwait's international airport and killing one person.

Kuwait's military confirmed that Iranian drones struck a passenger terminal at the airport, causing significant damage and wounding several people. The Kuwaiti defense ministry spokesperson Brigadier General Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan described the attack as "criminal Iranian aggression which resulted in significant material damage to the building and injuries." Civil aviation authorities suspended all air traffic at the airport and diverted incoming flights to alternative airports following the strike.

The attack came in response to earlier American military action. US forces fired a Hellfire missile at the M/T Lexie, a Botswana-flagged tanker, disabling its engine as it attempted to pass through international waters toward Iran's Kharg Island. The US military said the ship's crew had ignored repeated warnings over a 24-hour period. This marked the sixth vessel the American military has disabled since beginning its blockade of Iran on April 13, with 122 vessels redirected from Iranian ports altogether.

The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed it responded by attacking the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones. The US military's Central Command denied this claim. American forces reported they shot down three one-way attack drones launched by Iran and conducted strikes on an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island.

The IRGC said in a statement that US forces had struck an Iranian oil tanker near the strait of Hormuz with an aerial projectile, causing damage to its engine room. "These responses should serve as a lesson," the IRGC statement read.

The military escalation threatens ongoing efforts to negotiate a ceasefire agreement between Washington and Tehran. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio recently claimed that a deal with Iran was within reach, asserting that the regime had agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program previously off the table.

However, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi signaled the country would suspend peace talks in protest against Israeli offensive operations in Lebanon. He stated: "The ceasefire between Iran and the US is unequivocally a ceasefire on all fronts, including in Lebanon. Its violation on one front is a violation of the ceasefire on all fronts."

The latest exchange of strikes underscores the fragile state of regional security. Kuwait's position as a US ally that has historically maintained diplomatic relations with Iran makes the strike on its territory particularly destabilizing. The incident demonstrates how quickly the conflict can expand beyond direct US-Iran confrontation to affect neighboring nations and civilian infrastructure across the Persian Gulf region.

cards.headline: Karen Bass advances to runoff in Los Angeles mayor race
cards.teaser: Mayor Karen Bass will face a runoff election after advancing in the Los Angeles primary.
cards.body:
Incumbent Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass won the primary election but fell short of securing a majority of votes, forcing her into a November runoff. She will face one of two challengers: either Spencer Pratt, a former reality TV star and Republican newcomer, or Democrat city council member Nithya Raman.

Bass's primary victory reflects her standing as the leading candidate, though voters will determine her path forward in the general election runoff. The race highlights the competitive dynamics in California's largest city as residents weigh their choice for mayor.

cards.headline: Democrats gain ground in Iowa Senate and House primaries
cards.teaser: Iowa Democrats see potential for Senate seat pickup as primary results show rural comeback.
cards.body:
Democrats advanced candidates in Iowa primaries on Tuesday while setting their sights on competitive races across the state. An establishment Democrat won the Senate primary, positioning the party to challenge for a seat in the traditionally Republican-dominated state. A Trump-backed candidate lost in the gubernatorial race.

The party also celebrated primary victories by candidates Sand and Turek, marking what strategists view as a Democratic rural resurgence in Iowa. Democrats believe they can compete in three of Iowa's four House races, the Senate election, and the governor's contest as they seek to shift the balance of power heading into the November midterms.

cards.headline: California governor's race remains too close to call
cards.teaser: Top-two primary system leaves California's gubernatorial race undecided as vote counting continues.
cards.body:
California's primary election for governor stayed undecided as votes continued to be counted. Three candidates led the race early on: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer. The state's primary system allows all candidates to compete together regardless of party, with the top two vote-getters advancing to November's general election.

Two Democratic candidates, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan and former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa, conceded shortly after polls closed. With many ballots still outstanding, the final outcome remained uncertain.

cards.headline: White House launches immigration website comparing undocumented people to aliens
cards.teaser: A new White House website uses language referring to undocumented immigrants as extraterrestrials and says they do not belong.
cards.body:
Original Card (Unchanged)

The White House launched a website about immigration that compares undocumented immigrants to extraterrestrials. The site refers to people as 'it' and states 'they do not belong here,' according to reports.

The website represents a shift in how the administration publicly discusses immigration policy. The language choices drew attention for their framing of undocumented immigrants using terminology typically associated with science fiction rather than policy discourse.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones set St. Petersburg oil terminal ablaze
cards.teaser: Ukraine struck an oil facility in St. Petersburg as the city hosted an economic forum promoted by President Putin.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck an oil terminal in St. Petersburg early Wednesday, setting it ablaze as the city hosted an annual economic forum. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the attack. Several long-range drones reached their targets after Russian air defenses attempted to intercept them. Black smoke rose high above the city from the burning oil storage facilities.

The strike targeted energy and military sites ahead of President Putin's scheduled appearance at the economic forum on Friday. The timing underscores Ukraine's expanding drone operations into Russia's major cities, with St. Petersburg's distance from front-line fighting making it a notable target.

cards.headline: Copper theft rises as metal value increases
cards.teaser: Thieves target phone poles, streetlights, and EV chargers for copper as global prices climb.
cards.body:
Copper theft is increasing across the country as the value of the metal rises. Thieves strip copper from phone poles, streetlights, and electric vehicle chargers to sell for profit, creating costs for communities and infrastructure operators.

The thefts reflect growing demand and rising prices for copper, a metal used extensively in electrical systems and telecommunications infrastructure. The criminal activity disrupts services and requires expensive repairs to restore damaged equipment.

---

hero.headline: Oil prices rise as US and Iran exchange military strikes
hero.body:
Oil prices increased following a new round of military exchanges between the United States and Iran, intensifying concerns about regional stability and energy supply disruptions in the Middle East.

Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main international airport, causing heavy damage and killing at least one person. The attack prompted Kuwait to briefly shut down the airport, a critical transportation hub in the region. The US responded with military strikes against Iranian positions, including sites on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed it attacked the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain with missiles and drones in response to the American strikes. The US military's Central Command denied that any of these attacks successfully struck their facilities.

This latest exchange underscores the fragility of ceasefire efforts between the two nations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed during a Senate hearing that a deal with Iran remained within reach, asserting that Tehran had agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program that it had previously refused to discuss.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi disputed claims of progress, stating that any violations of the ceasefire on one front constituted violations across all fronts, including Lebanon. He held the US and Israel responsible for consequences stemming from any ceasefire breaches.

The conflict pushed oil prices higher as markets reacted to the threat of disruptions in a region that supplies a substantial portion of global oil. The exchange of strikes came after the US fired a Hellfire missile at a tanker attempting to break through an American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

Energy market volatility reflects broader concerns about Middle East stability. The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development released a report warning that consequences from Middle East conflicts would likely be felt across the global economy for an extended period.

According to the OECD report, even if oil prices reach their peak in the near term, the global economy faces a slowdown this year. The combination of energy price volatility and supply concerns stemming from regional military tensions is expected to weigh on economic growth across multiple countries and sectors.

The military escalation represents a significant setback for diplomatic efforts to stabilize the region. The lack of political progress in resolving the broader Middle East crisis contradicts optimistic public statements from US officials about the prospects for negotiated settlements. Traders and investors have grown increasingly concerned that ongoing military tensions could further disrupt energy supplies and extend the period of economic uncertainty facing the world economy.

cards.headline: Trump administration announces tariffs on 59 countries over forced labor
cards.teaser: The administration plans to impose levies of up to 12.5 percent on countries that failed to crack down on goods made with forced labor.
cards.body:
The Trump administration plans to impose tariffs of up to 12.5 percent on 59 countries and the European Union. The duties target nations deemed to have failed to adequately address the production of goods using forced labor.

This announcement comes months after the Supreme Court struck down many of the administration's previous tariffs in February, dealing a significant legal blow to its trade agenda. Despite that setback, the administration is proceeding with this new round of trade measures.

cards.headline: Stock market reaches new record as AI companies drive gains
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 closed at another record high, with artificial intelligence stocks leading the rally.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 closed at another record high, with stock futures showing minimal movement following the gain. Artificial intelligence stocks continue to be the primary engine of the market rally, with these companies driving much of the broader index's recent strength.

Wall Street analysts point to the concentrated nature of current market gains, noting that the surge remains heavily focused on the AI sector rather than being broadly distributed across the market.

cards.headline: Marvell stock surges after Nvidia CEO predicts trillion-dollar potential
cards.teaser: Shares of Marvell Technology soared 32 percent after Nvidia's Jensen Huang said the company could reach a trillion-dollar valuation.
cards.body:
Marvell Technology stock climbed to a 52-week high, surging 32 percent in trading. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that Marvell could become the next trillion-dollar company, calling it an essential player in the technology sector.

Broadcom and Hewlett Packard Enterprise also reached 52-week highs during the same trading session. The gains reflect continued investor enthusiasm for companies positioned in the artificial intelligence and semiconductor industries.

cards.headline: Palo Alto Networks raises annual forecast on AI cybersecurity demand
cards.teaser: The cybersecurity company topped earnings expectations as artificial intelligence drives increased demand for security products.
cards.body:
Palo Alto Networks reported earnings that exceeded analyst expectations and raised its annual forecasts. The company cited strong demand for AI-driven cybersecurity products as customers increase spending on cyber defenses.

Despite the strong earnings performance and raised guidance, Palo Alto stock fell in trading. The company's revenue rose as organizations invested more heavily in cybersecurity measures to protect against evolving threats in an AI-powered environment.

cards.headline: SpaceX targets $1.75 trillion valuation in upcoming IPO
cards.teaser: The company plans an all-primary initial public offering next week, though some analysts value it at less than half the target.
cards.body:
SpaceX is aiming for a $1.75 trillion valuation in its upcoming initial public offering next week. The offering will be structured as an all-primary deal, with all shares being newly issued by the company rather than existing shares being sold.

Morningstar analysts value SpaceX at significantly less than the company's IPO target. The public offering could potentially increase Elon Musk's net worth to over $1 trillion, a development that has drawn criticism from Democratic lawmakers.

cards.headline: CBS News fires Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The former CBS Evening News anchor was removed after months of tensions between staff and the network's editor in chief.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley, a veteran 60 Minutes correspondent and former anchor of CBS Evening News, following a broader staff overhaul at the program. The network also terminated the show's executive producer, executive editor, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

During a staff meeting, Pelley directly criticized CBS News management and editor-in-chief Bari Weiss over the firings. His strong reaction reflected months of mounting tensions between the show's staff and Weiss's leadership at the network.

hero.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft launch RTX Spark processors for Windows laptops
hero.body:
Nvidia has launched a new "superchip" designed to bring advanced artificial intelligence capabilities directly to Windows laptops and desktop computers. The RTX Spark processor represents the company's entry into the consumer PC market, putting it in direct competition with Intel, Apple, Qualcomm and AMD.

The chip will be available this year and will be used by major computer manufacturers including Dell, Lenovo, Asus and HP, paired with Microsoft's Windows software. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced the development at the Computex conference in Taiwan, describing it as a reimagining of the PC "for the first time in 40 years" following three years of collaboration with Microsoft.

The RTX Spark combines a microprocessor and graphics chip, developed with support from Taiwan's MediaTek. It is designed to run AI agents locally on devices rather than relying on cloud computing. According to Nvidia, the chip will enable AI agents to navigate PCs autonomously, potentially replacing traditional mouse and keyboard interactions. The company emphasizes that despite its power, computers using the processor will remain thin and lightweight.

Neil Shah, a co-founder of Counterpoint Research, compared the RTX Spark's potential impact to major technological milestones including the iPhone and ChatGPT, saying it could "transform the traditional app-centric PC to a real useful agentic AI personal computer which will eventually be in every home in coming years."

Nvidia is simultaneously expanding its CPU offerings with the Vera processor, designed for AI agents and adopted by early users including OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX. These moves demonstrate the company's broader strategy to extend beyond graphics cards and data center chips into integrated solutions that power entire computers.

The launch reflects growing demand for devices capable of running sophisticated AI applications locally without constant internet connectivity. Industry analysts view the move as strategically significant, though they note it represents a longer-term growth opportunity rather than an immediate earnings driver for the company.

The competition is intensifying as other chipmakers develop AI-focused processors. Intel announced plans to ship its own AI chip later this year featuring cheaper memory and cooling technology, along with a new graphics processor codenamed Crescent Island. Anil Nanduri, vice-president of AI products at Intel's Data Center Group, said the new processor is "purpose-built for this upcoming AI generation of agents."

When discussing AI's impact on employment, Huang dismissed concerns that the technology would reduce jobs, calling such fears "complete nonsense." He argued that AI would instead increase demand for software engineers by making workers more productive and enabling companies to expand their engineering teams.

The RTX Spark launch marks a significant moment in Nvidia's evolution from a graphics card manufacturer to a broader semiconductor company competing across multiple segments of the computing market.

cards.headline: Xcimer Energy activates world's largest privately owned laser
cards.teaser: The fusion startup turned on its laser system as part of efforts to develop commercial fusion energy.
cards.body:
Xcimer Energy has activated the world's largest privately owned laser as it develops commercial fusion energy technology using laser-based systems.

The milestone marks progress for the fusion startup, which competes alongside other private companies now investing in fusion research alongside government-funded programs that have traditionally led the field.

cards.headline: SpaceX veterans assess Blue Origin launch pad rebuild timeline
cards.teaser: Former SpaceX employees offered their perspective on how long repairs might take after damage to Blue Origin's launch facility.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday night. SpaceX veterans consulted about the rebuild effort described the situation at the site as difficult for those involved.

Launch pad construction and repair require specialized expertise and can take months or years depending on the extent of damage. The scope of repairs needed at Blue Origin's facility will ultimately determine how long the recovery process takes.

cards.headline: Male bowerbirds use human-made objects to attract mates
cards.teaser: Research shows the birds increasingly prefer bright manufactured items over natural materials in their courtship displays.
cards.body:
Male bowerbirds have begun incorporating human-made objects into the elaborate displays they build to attract females. Researchers observed the birds selecting bright manufactured items over traditional natural materials.

Scientists noted the behavior demonstrates how human activity is influencing animal behavior in unexpected ways. The birds' preference for colorful synthetic materials reflects their adaptation to environments increasingly shaped by human presence.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity firm Cyera seeks $12 billion valuation in new funding round
cards.teaser: The company is close to raising $300 million despite reporting operating losses.
cards.body:
Cyera is nearing completion of a $300 million funding round led by Evolution Equity Partners that would value the cybersecurity company at $12 billion. This valuation represents an 80 times multiple of the company's annual recurring revenue.

The data security specialist has attracted investor interest despite operating losses. The high valuation reflects broader corporate spending on cybersecurity tools as organizations prioritize data protection.

cards.headline: Sony announces God of War Laufey focusing on character Faye
cards.teaser: The PlayStation 5 game will explore the story of Kratos' wife from the God of War series.
cards.body:
Sony has officially announced God of War Laufey, a new PlayStation 5 title centered on Faye, the wife of series protagonist Kratos. The game was revealed during Sony's State of Play showcase, confirming earlier reports about the project.

Santa Monica Studio is developing the spinoff, which diverges from the main God of War series by shifting focus to a new character. Sony has stated the game is coming soon but has not announced a specific release date.

cards.headline: Insomniac Games reveals Wolverine gameplay details and features
cards.teaser: Developers discussed combat mechanics, X-Men character appearances, and a reduced-violence option for the upcoming game.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games showed new footage of its Wolverine game and explained key features. The developers confirmed X-Men characters will appear in the game, and players will be able to use Wolverine's claws in combat. The game will also include a low-gore option for players who prefer less graphic violence.

Developers also addressed how the character Logan can die during gameplay. The game footage demonstrated what observers described as high levels of violence consistent with the character's brutal fighting style.

hero.headline: Patriots Acquire Wide Receiver A.J. Brown from Eagles in Blockbuster Trade
hero.body:
The New England Patriots have acquired wide receiver A.J. Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles in a trade that reshapes both teams' offensive outlook. Brown participated in his first Patriots practice during organized team activities following the completion of the deal. The transaction drew mixed reactions at Eagles OTAs as Philadelphia parts ways with one of its top offensive weapons.

The trade brings a proven playmaker to New England's receiving corps, though analysis from multiple outlets suggests the move comes with significant considerations for the Patriots. Brown has established himself as one of the league's premier receivers, and his addition gives New England's offense a clear number one target. The Patriots made the move to address their ongoing need for elite talent at the position.

For Philadelphia, the departure of Brown marks a shift in the Eagles' offensive strategy. The team's reaction at organized team activities reflected the impact of losing a key contributor. Brown had been a central figure in Philadelphia's passing attack, and his exit leaves questions about how the Eagles will redistribute targets among their remaining receivers.

The Patriots received Brown in exchange for compensation that included draft picks and potentially additional assets, though the full details of what New England surrendered were outlined in reports examining the trade's implications. Analysts have debated whether the acquisition represents positive value for the Patriots given the cost, with some suggesting the price was steep for a team still building its roster.

Brown's arrival in New England comes as the Patriots continue their efforts to return to championship contention. His presence at OTAs allowed coaches and teammates to begin integrating him into the offensive system. The trade represents one of the more significant moves in the NFL offseason, affecting the competitive balance in both the AFC and NFC as teams prepare for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Myles Garrett Trade to Rams Required More Than Money for Jersey Number
cards.teaser: Browns defensive end Myles Garrett paid significantly to acquire his preferred number 95 jersey from the Rams after the blockbuster trade.
cards.body:
Myles Garrett paid a significant sum to acquire the Los Angeles Rams' No. 95 jersey following his trade from the Cleveland Browns. The star defensive end publicly acknowledged the expense, describing it as costing him "more than a couple bucks" to secure the number from its previous wearer.

The Browns general manager identified acquiring defensive end Jared Verse as a crucial component of facilitating the Garrett trade. The deal has generated substantial debate among NFL analysts regarding whether adding Garrett strengthens the Rams' Super Bowl prospects despite the considerable cost involved.

cards.headline: Retired Defensive Tackle Aaron Donald Considers NFL Return After Rams Acquire Garrett
cards.teaser: Former Rams star Aaron Donald is mulling a return to the NFL after Los Angeles completed its trade for Browns defensive end Myles Garrett.
cards.body:
Aaron Donald has broken his silence on the possibility of coming out of retirement following the Rams' acquisition of Myles Garrett. The retired defensive tackle is considering a comeback after the blockbuster trade that brought another elite defensive player to Los Angeles.

Rams head coach Sean McVay discussed the team's pursuit of Garrett and addressed the possibility of Donald returning to the roster. Donald's potential comeback has generated significant attention across the league, as he retired as one of the most dominant defensive players in NFL history. The addition of Garrett appears to have influenced Donald's thinking about whether to rejoin his former team.

cards.headline: Golden Knights Rally to Win Game 1 of Stanley Cup Final Against Hurricanes
cards.teaser: Vegas mounted another comeback to defeat Carolina in the opening game of the 2026 Stanley Cup Final.
cards.body:
Tomas Hertl broke a third-period tie to lift the Vegas Golden Knights past the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup Final on Tuesday in Raleigh. The victory continued Vegas's pattern of comeback wins, as the Knights erased an early two-goal deficit. Shea Theodore led the charge with three points, while Brett Howden, Ivan Barbashev, and William Karlsson also scored for the Golden Knights.

Carolina's strong start unraveled in the final period as Vegas found its rhythm. The Hurricanes' early two-goal advantage proved insufficient as the Knights capitalized on their opportunities. With the win, Vegas moved three victories closer to claiming their second Stanley Cup title.

cards.headline: Charles Leclerc Signs New Long-Term Contract with Ferrari
cards.teaser: Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc has agreed to a new long-term deal ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix.
cards.body:
Charles Leclerc has agreed to a new multi-year contract with Ferrari, extending his partnership with the team he has driven for since 2019. The 28-year-old Monegasque will continue alongside Lewis Hamilton, who also holds a long-term deal with the Scuderia.

Ferrari announced the agreement ahead of this weekend's Monaco Grand Prix, Leclerc's home race. With 155 races for the team, Leclerc has logged the second-most appearances for Ferrari in the team's history, behind only Michael Schumacher's legendary tenure from 1996 to 2006.

cards.headline: Aston Villa Forward Kirsty Hanson Set to Join Tottenham
cards.teaser: Aston Villa's top scorer Kirsty Hanson is joining Tottenham after an impressive Women's Super League season.
cards.body:
Kirsty Hanson is set to join Tottenham from Aston Villa after an impressive season in the Women's Super League. The forward was Aston Villa's top scorer during the campaign.

The transfer marks a significant move for Hanson, who has established herself as a key player at the top level of English women's football.

cards.headline: Bournemouth Midfielder Alex Scott Poised for England Debut in World Cup Friendlies
cards.teaser: Alex Scott is set to make his first appearance for England in upcoming World Cup warm-up matches in the United States.
cards.body:
Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is set to earn his first England cap in the upcoming World Cup warm-up matches taking place in the United States. The friendlies will serve as final preparation for the tournament.

England's squad has begun their World Cup preparations, with 21 of Thomas Tuchel's 26-man squad currently training at a camp in West Palm Beach, Florida. The squad numbers were confirmed this week, with midfielder Jude Bellingham receiving the coveted No 10 shirt. The team has expressed strong confidence ahead of their opening World Cup fixture in two weeks.

hero.headline: Singer Peabo Bryson Dies, Known for Disney Songs Beauty and the Beast and A Whole New World
hero.body:
Singer Peabo Bryson has died, according to statements from fellow musicians. Celine Dion expressed her grief over the loss of her collaborator, describing herself as heartbroken by his death. Bryson was best known for performing romantic ballads featured in Disney animated films.

Bryson gained widespread recognition for his work on Disney soundtracks during the 1990s. He performed A Whole New World from the 1992 film Aladdin with Regina Belle, and Beauty and the Beast from the 1991 film of the same name with Celine Dion. Both songs became signature works in his career and reached audiences worldwide through the popularity of the Disney films.

The collaboration between Bryson and Dion on Beauty and the Beast helped establish both artists in mainstream popular culture. The song appeared in the animated feature that became a cultural phenomenon and was later adapted into a successful Broadway musical and live-action film. A Whole New World similarly became one of the most recognized songs from the Disney animated catalog.

Bryson built his career as a vocalist specializing in romantic ballads and duets. His voice became associated with some of the most memorable movie songs of the late 20th century. The Disney tracks represented career highlights that introduced his work to generations of listeners through family entertainment.

Celine Dion's public statement about Bryson's death reflects the close working relationship the two singers maintained. Their recording of Beauty and the Beast remains one of the most successful duets in both of their discographies. The cause and circumstances of Bryson's death have not been detailed in available reports.

cards.headline: CBS News Fires 60 Minutes Correspondent Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: Scott Pelley issued a statement criticizing CBS leadership after being removed from the news magazine program.
cards.body:
CBS News fired Scott Pelley from his position as a correspondent on 60 Minutes following a broader overhaul of the show. The network had previously dismissed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two other correspondents, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

In a heated staff meeting, Pelley criticized CBS News management over the changes, directly targeting Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief. Pelley released a statement saying the principles he held dear were gone and that the leadership of 60 Minutes was no longer recognizable, prompting his departure from the program.

cards.headline: Two Thirds of Americans Play Video Games Weekly, Industry Report Says
cards.teaser: The Entertainment Software Association released data showing widespread video game participation across age groups.
cards.body:
Nearly 70 percent of Americans play video games for at least one hour each week, according to a report from the Entertainment Software Association. The figure encompasses 212.3 million people in the United States between ages 5 and 90.

The findings demonstrate that video games have become a widespread form of entertainment across multiple generations and demographic groups. The ESA collected the data as part of its research into gaming habits throughout the country.

cards.headline: Giorgio Locatelli to Co-Host Celebrity MasterChef After John Torode Exit
cards.teaser: The Italian restaurateur will join Grace Dent on the cooking competition series.
cards.body:
Giorgio Locatelli will replace John Torode as co-host of Celebrity MasterChef, the BBC announced. Locatelli, an Italian restaurateur, will appear alongside Grace Dent on the celebrity edition of the cooking competition program.

Torode left the show last year after serving as a host. Locatelli brings restaurant industry experience to the hosting role. The format of Celebrity MasterChef features well-known personalities competing in cooking challenges judged by culinary professionals.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass Advances to November Runoff
cards.teaser: The incumbent mayor will face another election after results from the primary vote.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advanced to the November runoff election after winning the primary with less than 50% of the vote. As the incumbent, she secured the most votes but fell short of an outright majority, necessitating a general election to determine the next mayor.

Bass will face one of two challengers in November. Reality television star Spencer Pratt and city council member Nithya Raman both advanced through the primary voting. As of Tuesday evening, it remained uncertain which challenger would ultimately compete against Bass in the general election.

cards.headline: Indian Film Board Clears The Voice of Hind Rajab for Release After Initial Block
cards.teaser: The Oscar-nominated film was initially censored in March amid concerns about diplomatic relations.
cards.body:
The Central Board of Film Certification in India reversed its decision to block The Voice of Hind Rajab, clearing the film for release. Director Kaouther Ben Hania's Oscar-nominated feature was initially censored by Indian authorities in March, sparking weeks of debate over the decision.

The film tells the story of a real person and had been blocked over concerns about its political sensitivity. Reports indicated fears that the theatrical release would affect diplomatic relations between India and Israel. The reversal allows the film to proceed with distribution in India after the initial censorship generated attention.

cards.headline: Hugo Blick Creates California Avenue Drama Series for BBC
cards.teaser: The show stars Helena Bonham Carter and Bill Nighy in what the producer describes as a tribute to 1970s television.
cards.body:
Hugo Blick created a new BBC drama series called California Avenue featuring actors Helena Bonham Carter and Bill Nighy. A producer on the show described it as a love letter to television from the 1970s.

Blick previously created several dramas including The English with Emily Blunt, The Honourable Woman starring Maggie Gyllenhaal, and Black Earth Rising featuring Michaela Coel. California Avenue continues his work in television drama with another cast of established actors. The series draws inspiration from the style and format of television programming from decades earlier.

hero.headline: Trump administration drops anti-weaponization fund after Senate GOP pushback
hero.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the Trump administration will abandon an $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund that faced mounting criticism from Senate Republicans and legal challenges. The decision removes a major obstacle to passing a $72 billion legislative package.

"We are not moving forward with the fund. Period," Blanche told House members, signaling the administration's reversal on the controversial initiative.

The fund, announced last month as part of a settlement in Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over leaked tax returns, was designed to compensate what the administration described as victims of politicized prosecutions. However, the proposal quickly drew fire from multiple directions. The fund lacked clear disclosure requirements about how money would be distributed and to whom, raising transparency concerns among Republicans who worried about potential political favoritism.

Senate Republicans, including Majority Leader John Thune, expressed particular alarm over the fund's structure and lack of oversight. Some GOP lawmakers pressed the White House to commit to abandoning the effort entirely. "I do think the best way to handle it is if the administration decides to shut the fund down themselves," Thune told reporters.

A significant source of Republican concern was the possibility that pardoned January 6 Capitol rioters could receive payments from the fund. Vice President Mike Pence called this prospect "deeply offensive" and said the sentiment was widely shared among Republicans and Americans generally.

The political backlash extended across the political spectrum. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer described the fund as "corruption in broad daylight" and vowed Democrats would force Senate Republicans to vote on measures to block payments. Several Democratic-led states, including California, Illinois, New York, and Connecticut, proposed measures to tax or block any distributions to their residents.

The administration also faced legal challenges. U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema in Virginia temporarily blocked the administration from transferring money from the fund after Democracy Forward filed a lawsuit seeking to dissolve it.

Some reports indicated the Justice Department had paused the program to comply with court orders, while Trump may have been reconsidering whether to continue pursuing the fund, multiple news outlets reported.

The reversal represents one of the few instances where Trump has yielded to pressure from Senate Republicans on a significant policy matter. The decision to abandon the fund removes a key barrier to advancing the broader legislative package, which Senate GOP leaders had indicated could not move forward with the fund included.

The episode illustrates ongoing tensions between the White House and Capitol Hill Republicans over spending priorities and executive authority, even as the party controls both branches of government. Senate Republicans have demonstrated willingness to challenge administration proposals they view as overreaching, particularly mechanisms involving discretionary funding that could bypass traditional appropriations oversight.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead California governor primary as votes counted
cards.teaser: Republicans and Democrats are selecting their nominees to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom in California's gubernatorial race.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra held leads as California counted votes in its governor primary. The race determines which two candidates advance to the general election to replace term-limited Gov. Gavin Newsom.

California's top-two primary system allows all candidates to compete together regardless of party affiliation. Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer also competed alongside Becerra, while Republican Chad Bianco challenged Hilton. Vote counting was expected to take several days due to California's slow tabulation process.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. If elected in November, she would make history as the first female Native American to serve as a state governor.

Haaland's primary victory secures her position as the Democratic nominee in a state where Democrats have recently held the governorship.

cards.headline: Midwest farmers face economic pressure as tariffs and war costs mount
cards.teaser: Rising costs from Trump's tariffs and the Iran war are testing a key Republican voting bloc ahead of November's midterm elections.
cards.body:
Farmers in the Midwest are experiencing economic strain from President Trump's tariffs and rising costs related to the Iran war, creating uncertainty for a demographic that strongly backed Republicans in recent elections. Trump won all but 11 of 444 farming-dependent counties in 2024.

The economic pressures come as Republicans seek to maintain control of Congress in the November midterm elections. Farmers represent a key voting bloc in several competitive Midwest districts and states, where agricultural issues often determine electoral outcomes.

cards.headline: House Democrats divided over Lebanon war powers vote
cards.teaser: Rep. Rashida Tlaib's resolution to constrain Trump from joining Israel's war in Lebanon has sparked internal party conflict.
cards.body:
An upcoming House vote on restricting the Trump administration from joining Israel's war in Lebanon is sparking frustration among Democrats. Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the resolution, but some party members are upset about being forced to take a position on the contentious measure.

The internal conflict reflects broader disagreement within the Democratic Party over Middle East policy and war powers authority. The divisive vote could significantly impact the resolution's chances of passing with Democratic support.

cards.headline: Trump's imprint grows on America's 250th birthday celebration
cards.teaser: The White House has created highly visible, centrally controlled events for the anniversary, many established by presidential directive.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

The White House has built a set of highly visible, centrally controlled events for America's 250th birthday celebration, with many created by presidential directive. The planning emphasizes spectacle, branding and new traditions under Trump's direction.

The approach marks a shift in how the milestone anniversary is being organized, with greater White House involvement in shaping the events and messaging around the celebration. The administration has prioritized creating events that center on presidential authority and visibility.

cards.headline: New Medicaid work requirements raise coverage concerns for low-income patients
cards.teaser: A rule explaining how states must implement work requirements may make it harder for sick people to maintain health coverage.
cards.body:
The administration released a rule guiding 42 states and Washington D.C. on implementing Medicaid work requirements. Critics worry the policy may make it harder for low-income sick people to maintain health coverage.

Republican lawmakers and administration officials have framed work requirements as a way to encourage employment among Medicaid recipients. The rule's implementation details—including how states will verify work activity and which exemptions will apply—will significantly affect people unable to meet the requirements.
